messages.subject: Customer Complaint — Ridgeline Apparel Co. Activation at Vancouver Community Trail Day
messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Worth flagging: we've had a complaint come in (ticket ZD-42098) from a participant at the Vancouver Community Trail Day regarding the Ridgeline Apparel Co. activation.

Short version: they felt the activation staff were overly pushy about collecting email signups and one participant says they were added to Ridgeline Apparel Co.'s mailing list without explicitly opting in. They're not happy and are asking us to remove them.

I've already handled the removal request on our end but the Ridgeline Apparel Co. signup is outside our system — that one's on their team.

Thought you should know before it goes any further, especially since we're mid-renewal discussions. Do you want to raise it with Marcus directly or would you prefer I handle it at the support level?

Cheers, E

messages.body:
Hey Ethan,

I've drafted the Ridgeline Apparel Co. sponsorship proposal for next season. Before I send it to Marcus I'd like a second set of eyes — specifically on the community metrics section since that's your data.

messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Now that we've had a couple days to breathe — here's my quick debrief on the Whistler Spring Series:

What went well:
- Registration flow was smooth, no major queues
- Cascadia Outdoor Gear activation got a lot of foot traffic, Fiona seemed really happy
- Community engagement on socials was up — I'll pull the full numbers this week
- Zendesk ticket volume post-event was low (only 3 complaints, all minor)

What needs work:
- The morning briefing ran 15 mins over — need a harder cutoff next time
- One participant had a gear issue that wasn't covered in the pre-event comms (I've updated the FAQ)
- Signage at the second checkpoint was confusing — a few people went the wrong way

Overall I think it was a strong event. Fiona already asked about renewal — did you get that email?

Cheers, E

They've asked for a partial refund.

This is probably one for you and Avery to weigh in on. Thoughts?

Cheers, E

Draft 2 of the Pacific Rim Coastal Traverse event brief is ready for review. This is the version that'll go to all sponsors and vendors so I want to make sure the community and customer-facing sections are accurate.

Section 4 looks good. Minor tweak: I'd say 'we'll promote across all owned channels' rather than listing them individually — we've added a few since the last brief template was made.

messages.subject: Post-Event Debrief — Vancouver Community Trail Day
messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Now that we've had a couple days to breathe — here's my quick debrief on the Vancouver Community Trail Day:

What went well:
- Registration flow was smooth, no major queues
- NorthPoint Hydration activation got a lot of foot traffic, Dale seemed really happy
- Community engagement on socials was up — I'll pull the full numbers this week
- Zendesk ticket volume post-event was low (only 3 complaints, all minor)

What needs work:
- The morning briefing ran 15 mins over — need a harder cutoff next time
- One participant had a gear issue that wasn't covered in the pre-event comms (I've updated the FAQ)
- Signage at the second checkpoint was confusing — a few people went the wrong way

Overall I think it was a strong event. Dale already asked about renewal — did you get that email?

Cheers, E

Hey Jordan,

Now that we've had a couple days to breathe — here's my quick debrief on the Squamish February Summit:

What went well:
- Registration flow was smooth, no major queues
- Basecamp Coffee Roasters activation got a lot of foot traffic, Sasha seemed really happy
- Community engagement on socials was up — I'll pull the full numbers this week
- Zendesk ticket volume post-event was low (only 3 complaints, all minor)

What needs work:
- The morning briefing ran 15 mins over — need a harder cutoff next time
- One participant had a gear issue that wasn't covered in the pre-event comms (I've updated the FAQ)
- Signage at the second checkpoint was confusing — a few people went the wrong way

Overall I think it was a strong event. Sasha already asked about renewal — did you get that email?

Cheers, E

messages.subject: Customer Complaint — Cascadia Outdoor Gear Activation at Vancouver Community Trail Day
messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Worth flagging: we've had a complaint come in (ticket ZD-75191) from a participant at the Vancouver Community Trail Day regarding the Cascadia Outdoor Gear activation.

Jordan

messages.subject: Post-Event Debrief — Squamish February Summit
messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Now that we've had a couple days to breathe — here's my quick debrief on the Squamish February Summit:

What went well:
- Registration flow was smooth, no major queues
- WildRoot Nutrition activation got a lot of foot traffic, Theo seemed really happy
- Community engagement on socials was up — I'll pull the full numbers this week
- Zendesk ticket volume post-event was low (only 3 complaints, all minor)

What needs work:
- The morning briefing ran 15 mins over — need a harder cutoff next time
- One participant had a gear issue that wasn't covered in the pre-event comms (I've updated the FAQ)
- Signage at the second checkpoint was confusing — a few people went the wrong way

Overall I think it was a strong event. Theo already asked about renewal — did you get that email?

Cheers, E

messages.subject: Post-Event Debrief — Pacific Rim Coastal Traverse
messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Now that we've had a couple days to breathe — here's my quick debrief on the Pacific Rim Coastal Traverse:

What went well:
- Registration flow was smooth, no major queues
- Cascadia Outdoor Gear activation got a lot of foot traffic, Fiona seemed really happy
- Community engagement on socials was up — I'll pull the full numbers this week
- Zendesk ticket volume post-event was low (only 3 complaints, all minor)

What needs work:
- The morning briefing ran 15 mins over — need a harder cutoff next time
- One participant had a gear issue that wasn't covered in the pre-event comms (I've updated the FAQ)
- Signage at the second checkpoint was confusing — a few people went the wrong way

Overall I think it was a strong event. Fiona already asked about renewal — did you get that email?

Cheers, E

messages.body:
Hey Jordan,

Worth flagging: we've had a complaint come in (ticket ZD-29484) from a participant at the Pacific Rim Coastal Traverse regarding the Basecamp Coffee Roasters activation.

Short version: they felt the activation staff were overly pushy about collecting email signups and one participant says they were added to Basecamp Coffee Roasters's mailing list without explicitly opting in. They're not happy and are asking us to remove them.

I've already handled the removal request on our end but the Basecamp Coffee Roasters signup is outside our system — that one's on their team.

Thought you should know before it goes any further, especially since we're mid-renewal discussions. Do you want to raise it with Sasha directly or would you prefer I handle it at the support level?

Cheers, E
